source.title: From Density Matrices to Phase Transitions in Deep Learning: Spectral Early Warnings and Interpretability

page_placements.theme: Developmental signatures of induction-circuit formation (LLC, susceptibilities, influence functions, spectra)

record.tranche_reason: Tests induction-head formation and its training-time phases using 2RDM spectral diagnostics and induction-head scores, rather than reproducing the original study’s measurement procedure.
record.gate_note: The induction-head experiment reports qualitative outcomes for SHC spikes, induction-head scores, an induction-benefit correlation, and eigenvector block-energy behavior. It does not report results for large transformers, other model families, few-shot task learning, or data/setup sweeps. Values appearing only in plots are not extracted as numbers. Results cited from other work are not recorded as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: Induction-head formation is a known transition used to validate the authors' 2RDM/SHC diagnostic. The results describe when SHC spikes and what its eigenvectors localise on. No induction-head score, loss, or in-context-learning value is reported, so no version's own effect is measured. The 'relatively sharp phase transition' line restates the expected outcome of the OEN+22 setup.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, but this is a claim about the diagnostic. The authors conclude that SHC consistently detects induction-head formation early and that its spikes and eigenvectors map onto known formation phases. They report three SHC spikes but describe the known structure as two-phase. They make no new claim about the induction-head mechanism or the phase change itself.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a small two-layer induction-head training setup and induction-head scores associated with the original work, but applies the new 2RDM/SHC diagnostics and an induction-benefit correlation. The tested transformer includes MLPs.
record.method_sensitivity: The probe set distinguishes repeated sequences, where induction can operate, from random sequences used as a control; the study reports that the leading eigenvector can switch between repeated-block and random-block modes around steps 1000–1300.

fits_no_version.finding: SHC rises before the induction-head score increase and before the LLC rise (Figs 4a, 14). Participation ratio leads SHC in induction-head formation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-covariance spectral statistics give early warning of induction-head formation in small transformers.

record.problems: The induction-head results are presented qualitatively in the text and figures, without numerical induction scores, correlation values, or uncertainty estimates. The experiment uses a small two-layer model and does not measure the loss-by-token-index criterion or a training-loss bump.
record.rows_left_out: No separate numerical values are extracted from the induction-head plots because the text provides no assignable numbers for them. Other 2RDM experiments and results cited from prior work do not bear directly on the claim versions tested here.

untested.parts: Composition with a previous-token head; the attention-only condition (the model includes MLPs).
Quantified abruptness of induction scores; coincidence with an in-context-learning gain and a loss bump.
Measured formation sub-steps; the SHC phases are mapped onto cited phases without independent measurement.
All; Appendix D suggests changing the data distribution, but this is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Induction-head results are qualitative: figures only, 30 seeds mentioned for Fig. 6a, no numbers. The reader's V1/V2/V7 labels are dropped because the study tests its tool, not the claim. The reader's V1 label also cited R3, which was not linked to V1.

versions.untested_parts: Tests induction-compatible attention behavior in a small two-layer transformer, but not composition with a previous-token head. The tested architecture includes MLPs, so the attention-only condition is not tested.
Does not test loss falling with token index, a bump in the training loss curve, or whether either coincides with an in-context-learning gain.
Large transformers and most in-context learning are not tested.
Other model families, sizes, runs as a universality claim, architectures, and modalities are not tested.
The study does not vary training data or setup to test their effects on induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Few-shot task learning and whether other mechanisms carry it are not tested.
The study interprets its observed SHC phases as corresponding to known phases, but does not identify or causally test every formation sub-step.

rows.subject: small causal transformer (induction-head experiment)
rows.size_stated: 2 layers, 4 attention heads per layer; dmodel = 128
rows.operation_detail: Measured per-head induction head scores, defined by attention to induction-compatible positions.

conditions.value: mixture of repeated [s∥s] sequences and uniformly random sequences

rows.measure: Induction head score / induction-compatible attention behavior over training
rows.value: The text describes induction-head formation as a relatively sharp phase transition with sudden attention-pattern reorganization; numerical scores are not stated.
rows.note: The score measures attention to positions compatible with the induction pattern, but does not test composition with a previous-token head.
rows.check: Induction scores appear only in Fig. 4a with no numbers. 'Relatively sharp phase transition' frames the OEN+22 setup rather than reporting a measured result. The score cannot show composition with a previous-token head, so V1 is not linked. The model has MLPs.

rows.subject: small causal transformer (induction-head experiment)
rows.size_stated: 2 layers, 4 attention heads per layer; dmodel = 128
rows.operation_detail: Tracked SHC across training using a sliding-window loss covariance.
rows.measure: Number and timing pattern of SHC spikes relative to induction-head formation
rows.value: The authors report generally three distinct SHC spikes and say they reflect the known phases of induction-head formation; the SHC is described as early-detecting formation.
rows.note: The multiple reported spikes qualify a single-transition account. The text does not establish coincidence with a token-index loss gain or a training-loss bump.
rows.check: SHC spikes are the study's own diagnostic signal, not a measure of induction-head formation sub-steps. The authors map three spikes onto a 'known two phase structure' from cited work without measuring the sub-steps. This is method performance, not evidence on V2 or V7.

source_check.problem: The row's note overinterprets multiple diagnostic spikes as evidence against a single formation transition; the third spike is attributed to an eigenvalue crossing.

rows.subject: small causal transformer (induction-head experiment)
rows.size_stated: 2 layers, 4 attention heads per layer; dmodel = 128
rows.operation_detail: Correlated the absolute top 2RDM eigenvector entries on repeated-sequence probes with each sequence’s induction benefit.

conditions.value: repeated [s∥s] sequences; random sequences used as control
first-half mean per-token cross-entropy minus second-half mean per-token cross-entropy

rows.measure: Correlation of |v1(i)| with induction benefit B(xi)
rows.value: The authors state that the correlation is high when the dominant loss-cofluctuation mode identifies samples by their sensitivity to the induction circuit; no numerical correlation is stated.
rows.note: The authors present this as evidence that the SHC spike reflects induction-head formation rather than only global statistical learning.
rows.check: This is a validation of the method: it checks whether the top eigenvector tracks induction benefit. It does not measure induction-head formation or in-context learning against a version. No correlation value is given.

rows.subject: small causal transformer (induction-head experiment)
rows.size_stated: 2 layers, 4 attention heads per layer; dmodel = 128
rows.operation_detail: Tracked top-eigenvector block energy for repeated and random probe groups.
rows.measure: Oscillation of top-eigenvector block energy and interpretation of leading-mode changes
rows.value: The text attributes oscillation to an eigenvalue crossing: a repeated-block capability mode decays as the induction circuit stabilizes, while a random-block residual-fitting mode grows; near-degenerate leading eigenvalues make the top eigenvector alternate between modes.
rows.note: This is the study’s stated interpretation of the third SHC increase and supports multiple distinct phases rather than one undifferentiated transition.
rows.check: The eigenvalue crossing (steps 1000–1300) reflects the optimizer shifting to fitting the random block after the circuit stabilises. It concerns the diagnostic's modes, not separate formation sub-steps, so it does not bear on V7.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.problem: The row's note overinterprets multiple diagnostic spikes as evidence against a single formation transition; the third spike is attributed to an eigenvalue crossing.

relation.reason: Induction-head scores and induction benefit serve as reference measurements for evaluating the new diagnostic.

tranche.reason: The experiment uses known induction-head formation to validate diagnostic timing and interpretability; it does not independently test a claim version.

source_check.notes: The pack's assertion that no induction-head score is reported needs correction: Figures 4a and 14 present scores graphically, although the extracted text supplies no numerical score values. Three SHC spikes do not establish three formation sub-steps; Section 3.2 interprets the third through an eigenvalue crossing.
